He was the only keeper on the board and the board still shows none. That makes the Neuer sale impossible: he is the squad's only goalkeeper, and selling him would leave no legal formation at all, which is a worse outcome than the negative balance the sale was meant to cure. So the Neuer leg is closed, not deferred. In its place: buy Ullrich, then sell Tanaka and Jeltsch. That structure clears the deficit on today's values without relying on a single market tick, keeps a legal eleven, and is points-POSITIVE rather than a sacrifice.

Jeltsch goes last and deliberately late: he is benched, so his sale costs no points, and he is on a rising flag with several ticks left before the lock, which makes patience worth real money. Hold him through the final tick, then sell with a clear margin before the lock — not in the lock hour.

buy.reason: Ullrich is the move, and he is doing two jobs at once: he is the extra body that licenses a second sale, and he is a genuine upgrade on the man he replaces. He is a fit, regular starter playing close to full matches, and he is cheap for that profile. The bid is set deliberately ABOVE market value. The flip discipline — bid exactly market value and never raise — is unchanged and still absolutely binds on flips, where any premium destroys the edge. Becker and Kosugi look tempting on points and are arithmetically excluded — either one leaves the balance negative at the lock, which scores zero for the whole matchday. Fullkrug remains the only real points upgrade on the board and remains unfinanceable: paying for him means selling one of the two best assets in the squad, which is a net loss of points.
